title: Build a checked C++ component

objectives.text: Implement a complete bounded single-symbol long-only confirmed-fill component with explicit validation/status/duplicate/funds policies and safe precommit arithmetic/resource ordering.

Reconcile accepted fills independently and test rejected-state immutability, retry policy and resource/exception limits without claiming durable transaction/account/settlement or app-runtime qualification.

blocks.markdown: Build one synthetic single-currency, single-instrument account starting flat, initial economic cash in [0,10^9] cents. Each already-confirmed Fill has positive int ID within one declared source/account namespace, signed quantity in [-10^6,10^6] excluding 0, positive price<=10^6 cents/share, fee in [0,10^6] cents. At most 1000 accepted fills; position must remain long-only in [0,10^6] and economic cash nonnegative. This is an own acceptance policy, not a broker execution/settlement protocol or permission to trade. No marks/realized basis/tax/FX/income/corporate/borrow/settlement functionality is implied.

Every rejected append returns a specific status and leaves cash/position/accepted-ID list unchanged. Validation runs first, then duplicate-ID rejection, capacity, proposed position and funding. Any repeated accepted ID is rejected even with identical payload; this policy deliberately differs from the earlier portfolio replay no-op policy and must not be silently swapped. Rejected IDs are not consumed, so a corrected retry of a previously rejected ID can later succeed. Correction/bust authentication and multi-source namespace merging need separate protocols.

The precommit arithmetic uses long long. Before each accepted operation, position is bounded by 10^6. A candidate position plus bounded delta lies in [-10^6,2*10^6], safe before its range check. Each absolute notional is at most 10^12 cents and fee at most 10^6. Over at most 1000 accepted fills, absolute cash is bounded by initial 10^9+1000*(10^12+10^6), well below the standard minimum signed long long maximum. A proposed next cash uses at most one more bounded operation before the capacity check prevents further acceptance, so no unbounded accumulation/abs(LLONG_MIN)/narrow product is evaluated. Changing these limits requires revisiting this proof.

blocks.title: Only accepted fills change the ledger

steps.text: Start 10000 cents, 0 shares. Accept ID1 buy 5 at 1000 fee 2: cash 4998, position 5, count 1.
Reject repeated ID1 as duplicate. Reject sell 9 because it would create a short position; both leave state unchanged.
Accept ID3 sell 2 at 1100 fee 1: cash 7197, position 3, count 2. Independent sums are 10000-5000-2+2200-1 and 5-2.
No successful fill is inferred from an order/target. These input records are confirmed under the synthetic source contract; a local component cannot authenticate that fact.

blocks.caption: Expected lines: 1, 1, 1, 1, then 7197 3 2. Boolean comparisons show each expected status. The complete component exposes read-only snapshots and validates before mutation. Accepted-ID append can allocate/throw; with int vector elements its failed push_back leaves the vector unchanged, and scalars are assigned only after successful append. This is in-memory exception behavior, not durable commit, crash atomicity or concurrency safety.

blocks.markdown: The vector<int> append is the only potentially throwing operation after domain validation. For this element type it has the strong exception guarantee; after successful append the long long assignments do not throw. No public partially committed state is exposed under this single-threaded model. Do not turn this argument into "all vector types/allocators or multi-record transactions are atomic". Allocation failure is an exception, not an ApplyStatus::funds business rejection. No forced allocation-failure injection is claimed by an ordinary successful local test.

blocks.caption: Expected output: ledger reconciled 7197 3, exit 0. A buy rejected for funds leaves every snapshot field unchanged and does not consume ID2; the later valid ID2 sell is accepted. The final cash/quantity reference uses independently written fixed-trace sums, not the exact mutation loop copied into a second helper. No broker statement or source completeness is validated by this synthetic reference.

blocks.markdown: Test valid buy/sell, zero/negative invalid fields, huge values rejected BEFORE multiplication, duplicate IDs, rejected retry, exact funding, insufficient cash, insufficient inventory, position cap and 1000/1001 capacity. Compare cash/quantity to a separate accepted-fill reference and require all rejection statuses preserve snapshots. Check constructor invalid cash. Replaying a successful batch into the same instance yields duplicates rather than applying again. Test empty/start state independently. Instrumented runs cover only those executed cases; account provenance, source completeness, persistence, synchronization and actual runner gates remain separate.

Independent transfer: add a read-only accepted-fill audit log rather than just IDs, preserving exception-safe ordering and capacity. Derive how that changes allocation/copy exceptions and resource bounds before claiming the same guarantee. Add a mark-only equity query without changing economic cash/position; state price/time/currency/short assumptions. Do not add a balancing event merely because an independent statement differs.

Sources: [Core Guidelines ownership/error/invariants](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines.html), [vector behavior](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector.html), and [instrumented-testing scope](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Instrumentation-Options.html). Integer/resource/status policies are explicit own synthetic contracts, not a real brokerage acceptance model. The exact [vector push_back exception contract](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector/push_back.html) supports the int-element ordering argument; no injected allocation-failure test is claimed.

summary: A checked component needs exact bounded arithmetic, identity/status policy, validation before commit and independent accepted-fill reconciliation. Rejected appends preserve state under the reviewed in-memory contract; durable/source/account/settlement/concurrency and app qualification remain separate.
